//: Baseline of KNOWN-NOT-PASSING core tests on a clean tree, captured to make "no new test failures" a trustworthy gate despite a non-deterministic (sharded, memory-pressured) suite.
capturedFrom: stableFailures retired 2026-09-21 after a clean full run showed all 90 passing; flakyFiles still carry the original 2-run intersection method, because one clean run is not evidence about flakiness under sharding.

flakyFiles.//: EMPTY. This held 12 whole files whose failures the gate ignored outright, described as passing in isolation but flaking under sharded memory pressure. Measured 2026-09-21: running them together 3 times, one run died with "[vitest-pool]: Worker forks emitted error / Worker exited unexpectedly" -- 10 of 11 files reported and 3 tests never ran. The flake was never a failing assertion, it was a WORKER CRASH, and the heaviest allocator among them (300,000 elements, 13 wall-clock assertions, and it writes a report file) was the cause. Moving the two benchmark suites behind HOLO_BENCH=1 and the two wall-clock bounds in RuntimeOptimization behind the same flag made 5 consecutive runs clean with zero crash lines. One entry, VRRPerformanceBenchmark.spec.ts, named a file that no longer exists. Quarantining twelve files CORRECTNESS to tolerate two benchmarks CRASHING was the wrong trade.
flakyFiles.retiredEvidence: 5 of 5 consecutive runs of all 11 existing files clean, 0 worker-crash lines, after gating the benchmarks; before gating, 1 of 3 runs crashed a worker.

serialPassFiles.//: SCHEDULING ONLY, NEVER A VERDICT. These files run in run-vitest.mjs pass 1 at --maxWorkers=1 and are excluded from the 4-way sharded pass 2, because they are memory- or timing-sensitive under shard pressure. A failure in one of them is still a failure: the ignore-list is flakyFiles.files above, and it is empty. These two jobs were conflated until 2026-09-22 -- the comment in run-vitest.mjs called flakyFiles 'the canonical list' while both consumers carried their own hardcoded copy, and all three had diverged. Read at runtime by run-vitest.mjs and vitest.config.ts; do not mirror it by hand. src/compiler/__tests__/VRRPerformanceBenchmark.spec.ts was dropped here: it named a file that no longer exists.

ciCoverageExclusions.//: SCHEDULING ONLY, CI COVERAGE RUNS. Excluded only when CI=true and --coverage, to keep 8GB runners alive. Separate from serialPassFiles: this list is about a coverage run's memory ceiling, not about shard flakiness. Read at runtime by vitest.config.ts.

stableFailures.//: EMPTY, and that is the point. This list held 90 entries described as "deterministic pre-existing failures"; on 2026-09-21 a clean full run of the core suite reported "total failures=0 | known-stable=0 | known-flaky=0 | NEW=0" -- not one of the 90 failed. 17 of them could not have: 10 named src/compiler/__tests__/MatterpakCompiler.test.ts, a file that no longer exists, and 7 named test titles that no longer exist either. 19 more were in marketplace-runtime.test.ts, which fails only because @holoscript/auth is unbuilt -- built it, and its 130 tests pass. The list was a fossil of a broken build environment, not a record of defects, and while it stood the gate accepted 90 named failures in advance. A NEW failure is now any failure at all, outside a flaky file.
stableFailures.retiredEvidence: corepack pnpm --filter @holoscript/core test:baseline, clean tree at 0882bc9b6, packages/auth and openusd-plugin built: total failures=0.
